title: Foam-Core Cement Panel
summary: A lightweight, insulating structural panel made from XPS foam core encapsulated in fiberglass mesh and Portland cement mortar. Suitable for non-load-bearing walls, countertops, decorative elements, and test panels.
use_cases: Test panels for mix ratio experiments

mixes.name: Base coat mortar
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1.5 parts fine sand
mixes.admixture: SikaLatex diluted 1:3 as mix water (replaces some water)

mixes.name: Finish coat
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1 part fine sand

steps: 1. Cut XPS foam to desired panel dimensions.
2. Score foam surface lightly with utility knife for adhesion.
3. Apply thin pegapiso bond coat to both faces — let tack.
4. Press AR fiberglass mesh into bond coat on both faces.
5. Apply base coat mortar (8–12mm total) over mesh using trowel.
6. Allow to firm up (2–4 hours), keep damp.
7. Apply finish coat (4–6mm) for smooth or textured surface.
8. Damp cure for minimum 7 days — cover with plastic or wet burlap.
risks: Foam is combustible — must be fully encapsulated. No exposed foam in finished work.
Thin mortar coats can crack if cured too fast — damp cure is mandatory.
Ordinary fiberglass cloth ≠ AR mesh — check the mesh rating.
safety_notes: Non-structural panel. Not for load-bearing, spanning, or inhabited-space structural use.
Foam releases toxic smoke if ignited — always fully encapsulate.
local_substitutions: EPS (unicel) can substitute for XPS — less rigid, similar process.
Diamond mesh can substitute for AR mesh — results in more traditional ferrocement finish.
supplier_notes: All materials available in Puerto Vallarta — COMEX, local ferreteras.
AR fiberglass mesh may need to be sourced from SIKA distributor or ordered.
expected_lifespan: 20+ years if properly sealed and maintained

title: Ferrocement Barrel Roof
summary: A curved thin-shell ferrocement roof formed over cattle panel or rebar ribs. Creates a self-supporting barrel vault. Requires local engineering review for any inhabited structure.

mixes.name: Ferrocement mortar
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1.5 parts fine sand
mixes.admixture: SikaLatex 1:3 as partial mix water. Target consistency: thick peanut butter.

steps: 1. Establish wall plates or beam ledges at correct span and height.
2. Bend cattle panel to barrel curve — secure ends to wall plates.
3. Add intermediate ribs if span > 3m.
4. Layer diamond mesh over cattle panel — secure with binding wire.
5. Add second mesh layer offset from first.
6. Optional: add AR fiberglass mesh as third layer.
7. Apply mortar from underside — work mortar fully through all mesh layers.
8. Allow underside to firm, then apply top coat.
9. Total shell thickness: 25–40mm.
10. Damp cure minimum 14 days. Cover with plastic and wet.
11. Apply waterproofing membrane to top surface after cure.
risks: STRUCTURAL — any inhabited space below requires local engineering review.
Shell thickness must be consistent — thin spots create failure points.
Barrel end thrust must be properly anchored at wall plates.
Puerto Vallarta is in a seismic zone — engineering review mandatory for inhabited structures.
safety_notes: ⚠️ ENGINEERING NOTE: This system involves a spanning roof. Any inhabited structure, load-bearing element, spanning roof, or elevated platform must be reviewed by a licensed local engineer and must comply with local building codes.
Do not use over inhabited spaces without engineering review and permit.
Scaffold and fall protection required during construction.
local_substitutions: Rebar ribs can substitute for cattle panel — more labor but locally available.
Chicken wire (gallinero) can work for small-span experimental structures — not for inhabited use.
supplier_notes: Cattle panel available from agricultural suppliers.
Diamond mesh and cement at local ferreteras.
Waterproofing: SIKA or Sherwin-Williams at COMEX.

title: XPS Kitchen Counter / Sink Counter
summary: A cast-in-place or precast concrete countertop formed over XPS foam substrate with integral undermount sink cavity. Waterproofed and sealed for kitchen and bathroom use.
tools: Hot wire foam cutter or utility knife

mixes.name: Base structural coat
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1 part fine sand

mixes.name: Finish slurry coat
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 0.5 parts fine sand

steps: 1. Cut XPS foam to counter profile, including sink cutout if needed.
2. Build up thickness with foam layers — target 40–60mm total substrate.
3. Apply pegapiso bond coat over foam — press AR mesh into it.
4. Wrap edges with mesh.
5. Apply base coat mortar — minimum 12mm over mesh.
6. Cure 48 hours damp.
7. Apply finish slurry coats — 2–3 thin passes.
8. Sand progressively (80→120→220→400 wet) after final cure.
9. Apply penetrating sealer — minimum 3 coats.
10. Install sink hardware and caulk perimeters.
risks: Waterproofing is critical — inadequate sealing causes staining and water damage.
Edge strength — edges must have sufficient cement thickness (minimum 12mm).
safety_notes: This is a countertop system — not structural.
Ensure the supporting cabinet structure can bear the weight of the cement counter.
local_substitutions: EPS can substitute for XPS core — less precision in cutting.
Diamond mesh can work in place of AR mesh for non-sink counters.
supplier_notes: Sealers: COMEX carries penetrating concrete sealers.
Wet-dry sandpaper available at auto parts stores or ferreteras.

title: Raised Bed System
summary: Foam-core cement panel raised garden beds. Lightweight, durable, and insulating for plant roots. Suitable for rooftop and ground-level gardens.
tools: Corner angle pieces (optional — for clean corners)

mixes.name: Panel mortar
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 2 parts fine sand

steps: 1. Cut foam panels to desired bed dimensions.
2. Apply mesh and mortar to all four panel faces (inside and outside).
3. Cure panels flat — minimum 7 days damp.
4. Assemble panels into box form — tie corners with mortar or bracket.
5. Apply corner fill mortar for sealing.
6. Final cure assembled bed — wet interior daily for 3 days.
7. Interior can receive a food-safe waterproof coating if desired.
risks: Foam exposed on interior edges — must seal against plant moisture for longevity.
Rooftop use: verify structural capacity before placing heavy planted beds.
safety_notes: Lightweight system — no engineering review needed for standard ground-level beds.
Rooftop: verify building structural capacity for wet soil load.
local_substitutions: EPS (unicel) works as form core — less precise but available everywhere.
supplier_notes: All materials at COMEX and local ferreteras.

title: Outdoor Kitchen System
summary: Full outdoor kitchen build using foam-core cement counter, concrete block base, tile finish, and integrated grill/stove area. Non-structural kitchen elements over a masonry base.

mixes.name: Counter top mortar
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1 part fine sand

steps: 1. Lay concrete block base for counter height (typically 90cm).
2. Build out counter depth with blocks.
3. Cap with foam-core cement counter panel (see xps-kitchen-counter system).
4. Tile or stucco the block base faces.
5. Install grill or stove cutout with proper clearance.
6. Apply waterproofing to all counter surfaces.
7. Seal and finish.
risks: Fire clearances around grill — follow appliance manufacturer specifications.
Moisture management critical in Puerto Vallarta humidity.
safety_notes: Non-structural countertop — counters do not span or carry loads.
Gas line connections require licensed plomero/gas technician.
Grill clearances: minimum 30cm clearance from combustible materials above grill.
supplier_notes: Block available from local block manufacturers (block producers in PV are everywhere).
Tile from tile warehouses on the highway.

title: Bathroom / Tub / Shower Form
summary: Waterproof cement shell shower pan and surround built over foam form. Replaces traditional tile over cement board with a monolithic waterproof foam-cement system.
tools: Hot wire cutter or utility knife
Spray bottle or misting system for curing

mixes.name: Shell mortar
mixes.ratio: 1 part Portland cement : 1 part fine sand

steps: 1. Form foam to shower pan shape — create positive slope (1% minimum) to drain.
2. Coat all foam surfaces with AR mesh + mortar (minimum 12mm).
3. Form shower walls over foam or over existing structure.
4. Apply minimum 3 mortar coats total to water-exposed surfaces.
5. Apply dedicated waterproofing membrane over cured shell.
6. Test with flood test (plug drain, fill with water 24hr) before tiling.
7. Tile or leave raw cement finish with penetrating sealer.
risks: Waterproofing failure leads to structural moisture damage — do NOT skip flood test.
Slope errors create standing water and mold conditions.
safety_notes: Shower and wet room surfaces must be fully waterproofed — any breach causes long-term damage.
Non-structural application — shower surround does not span or carry loads.
supplier_notes: Waterproofing: SIKA or Sherwin-Williams waterproof coatings at COMEX.

title: Material Test Panel Protocol
summary: Standard protocol for casting, curing, and evaluating small test panels before committing to full-scale builds. Essential for calibrating mix ratios, mesh combinations, and surface finishes locally.
steps: 1. Record date, weather conditions, and all material sources and batch numbers.
2. Prepare a 300mm x 300mm (12"x12") test panel form.
3. Mix test batch per target ratio — record exact ratios.
4. Apply to form with target technique (trowel, spray, press).
5. Record thickness at 4 corners.
6. Cure per test conditions (damp, dry, covered, uncovered — test one variable at a time).
7. At 7 days: inspect, photograph, record observations.
8. At 28 days: final inspection, scratch test, bend test if feasible.
9. Log all results in /data/beads.json linked to lab entry.
risks: Test panels only — do not use test panels as finished structural elements.
safety_notes: Test panels help avoid costly failures at full scale — always test first.
